decisions.reason: The original X=(x_1,...,x_M) and X_t=(x_1,...,x_t) identify candidate prefixes with observation histories: with X=(a,b), no initial data, and a first selection b, K_1 could use a instead. Candidate sites are now c_j and trace sites x_i, and the selected site and single returned value are appended together. Positive-definite observed covariance, repeated sites, zero-noise failure, t=0 and N=s branches, Cholesky solves, final update, least-index selection, and inherited AC are preserved. The true-posterior caveat now also excludes informative availability; otherwise only a surrogate kernel is asserted.

The two children had no specified creation/evaluation order. With N=2, the root and only one child are evaluated, so different permitted orders produce different recorded fields and incumbents. The procedure now evaluates the root first and, after each split, creates/evaluates the lower-half child before the upper-half child, finishing pending children before closure or another split. Coverage, call counting, retained bounds, midpoint witnesses, missing-field returns and singleton refinement are unchanged.

F6 incorrectly describes all processed open leaves while a child is pending; a new witness can lower U before the next closure sweep. The expanded box, however, is selected only after that sweep, so the proof needs F6 only at split checkpoints. F6 and step 4.1 now use that exact checkpoint. At expansion, ell(B_k)<U_k-epsilon<=f(midpoint(B_k))-epsilon; both endpoints converge to f(x), an immediate contradiction. Compact-image attainment, deterministic infinite-branch extraction without AC, longest-side shrinkage, and singleton-root exception remain sound. Statement is unchanged.

The original unconstrained root witness x=1 violated the midpoint instruction. With its original epsilon=1/2 the required midpoint is already epsilon-optimal, so that construction proves no failure. The repaired construction uses the mandated midpoint x=1/2, exact U=1/2, epsilon=1/4, N=1 and invalid ell=1/2. The single root call reports U-ell=0 although the true error is 1/2>1/4. It now follows every algorithm instruction except the deliberately invalid lower bound. Statement refuted is preserved; only Construction and Verification changed.

False positive: the Statement expressly assumes all operation results are finite, and the operation definition classifies split-domain as a status, not a finite interval. The proposed DAG gives x*x=[-4,4], then [-3,5], so its division returns split-domain and violates that hypothesis. The theorem does not promise a finite result merely from separation of exact denominators. For successful finite evaluations, outward input rounding and DAG induction enclose every exact value. For shrinking boxes with increasing precision and no overflow, input and constant widths vanish, arithmetic endpoint maps converge, and denominator enclosures eventually exclude zero. The fixed-L Lipschitz estimate q_- - L r^+ is valid and converges as the radius and rounding error vanish. No carrier or contract edit is needed.

A zero-dimensional continuous box was admissible but its spatial fallback requires n>=1. The repair preserves purely integer inputs by replacing the singleton empty continuous tuple by a dummy [0,0] coordinate before all supplier calls, ignoring it in objective/constraint DAGs and projecting it away on return. This bijection preserves feasible points, bounds and ledgers. Also initialized root queue/ledger, integer residual budget and incumbent, specified witness updates and child order, and made fallback integer allocation explicit: R=Mq+h, first h budgets q+1 and remaining budgets q, q>=1. Median partitions, continuous coverage, verified dual-bound prerequisites, empty-node handling and total budget remain intact. Its fallback now also rejects pending/missing bounds, returns all-infeasible before taking a minimum, and preserves the no-incumbent sentinel when there are no witnesses.

The oracle explicitly permits non-finite statuses, but the old response branch handled only unavailable. Such a status has no lower-bound value and cannot enter the positivity or splitting tests. The procedure now returns inconclusive with the current queue/ledger before those tests for every unavailable or non-finite vector entry. It explicitly processes and removes the oldest entry only after a finite vector report, then certifies or replaces it by ordered children or its singleton refinement. One budget unit is a box query for the finite ordered constraint vector; every query, including refinements, is counted. Valid finite bounds and strict-positive pruning are preserved.

The numerical certificate is correct but the old example omitted the algorithm-required node budget. It now specifies N=3, with one root call and lower- then upper-child calls. Ordinary multiplication gives root t,u=[-1,1] and root f=[-2,2], so U=0 cannot certify epsilon=9/10. Both children give lower -1 and midpoint objective -3/16. After three calls L=-1, U=-3/16, gap=13/16<9/10. Square completion gives minimum -1/4 at the two displayed interior points, so the witness error is 1/16. Contract finite-check text also needs its old root lower -1 corrected to -2.

The old F1 and step 2.1 omitted the integrality prerequisite needed by the spatial termination theorem, although allocation of a counted residual call budget has an elementary integer interpretation. They now explicitly use R=Mq+h with M=|Z|>=1, q=floor(R/M)>=1 and 0<=h<M, giving positive integer budgets q or q+1 with sum R. The proof also checks that dummy-singleton preprocessing makes every spatial subcall positive dimensional. Each subcall meets the finite-call spatial theorem, and its budget plus already charged main-tree calls totals at most N. Statement is unchanged; the missing prerequisite is now explicit.

F2 was an overbroad paraphrase: a factorable relaxation alone does not certify a lower bound. F2 now states the supplier hypotheses: nonempty real-hull feasible set, certified convex relaxation and coefficient/domain enclosures, a dual-feasible pair, and verified ell<=q. Step 2.1 checks nonemptiness using the feasible pair being bounded, then applies that certificate at its integer-feasible point; empty nodes need no infimum. Coverage and retained bounds are unchanged, and the dummy singleton maps bijectively back to zero continuous dimensions. The feasible incumbent and valid node bounds already in the Statement suffice for the gap argument, so this citation qualification repairs a nonfatal fact overstatement without changing the claim.
